self-host:blazephoenix-xyz.name: BlazePhoenix

out_of_scope.identifier: Third-party code the protocol reads from, unless our code consumes it unsafely
Volumetric DoS, load testing and rate-limit exhaustion of the free public API
Theoretical reports without a proof of concept

self-host:blazephoenix-xyz.summary: Covers an EVM DEX aggregator, a staking engine, and the public API, MCP server, SDK and website. Reports accepted 25 September to 7 November 2026 (23:59 UTC). Rewards are paid in the project's own token, not yet liquid, so the programme commits to a token quantity and schedule rather than a value; settlement begins after October 2026. Duplicates reported before a fix is published split one award equally. Severity is set by the project, with written reasoning where it differs from the reporter's.

self-host:matrix-org.name: Matrix.org Foundation

out_of_scope.identifier: Issues relating to SPF or DMARC

self-host:matrix-org.summary: The Matrix.org Foundation follows coordinated vulnerability disclosure for security issues in Matrix. Reports go to its security address, optionally PGP encrypted, and the team replies within five business days. It aims to fix within 90 days, or around 120 for especially complex issues, and may hold technical details for up to 30 days after a fix is public. Reporters may disclose once the issue is addressed, and are credited in the Security Hall of Fame. It does not ordinarily pay bounties.
